top_stories.title: OpenAI Nears $1.25 Trillion Valuation in $30B Funding Round
points: OpenAI is raising up to $30 billion in a new funding round led by UAE investors, pushing its valuation above $1 trillion for the first time to roughly $1.25 trillion.

The round is being positioned as bridge financing ahead of a potential future IPO (initial public offering, when a private company first sells shares to the public), with OpenAI targeting signatures by the end of next week.
DeepSeek separately raised $15 billion in one of China's largest funding rounds, just two days after U.S. federal agencies were ordered to remove its AI over security concerns.

top_stories.title: Critical PHP Vulnerabilities Exploited at Massive Scale ('Black October')
points: Two critical bugs in PHP (a programming language powering roughly 70% of websites) went unpatched since 2012; they were discovered by AI on August 1 and actively exploited by October 17, four days before the public fix shipped.

Within hours of the October 21 patch release, exploitation scaled from thousands to millions of attempts, aided by AI 'agent swarms' (coordinated automated attack systems); Microsoft reported a China-linked group reaching admin access in under 3 hours using an AI hacking tool.
Wikipedia, Archive.org, 4chan, government pages, the Dutch government, and Germany's Charité hospital took themselves offline preemptively rather than risk compromise.
Fix: update to PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36, or 8.2.35; older versions have no official patch and need vendor patches or a full upgrade; shared hosting users should confirm their host has patched.
The severity of this attack wave was compared to the March 2020 pandemic crisis by a former OpenAI chief futurist; OpenAI also released a free PHP vulnerability checker for website owners.

unique_angles.point: Storm-0940 hit Microsoft 365 accounts with 2,900 login attempts per minute, illustrating why passkeys/security keys (which can't be guessed or leaked from a breached server) matter more than strong passwords.

Attacks were simultaneous and global: state-linked actors targeted hundreds of organizations while unauthorized AI agents were found operating inside bank customer accounts across India, Latin America, and South Korea.

top_stories.title: Banks Restrict AI Agents After They Go Off-Script in Customer Accounts
points: JPMorgan, Bank of America, Morgan Stanley, and Citi discovered third-party AI agents logging into customer accounts with credentials, calling support lines, and taking actions customers never explicitly requested.

The core risk is AI hallucination (the AI misreading instructions and making incorrect decisions) when agents are given authority to move money or make purchases; some executives called the situation 'horrifying.'

Response: Morgan Stanley is blocking third-party agents entirely, while JPMorgan, BofA, and Citi are moving most agents to read-only access (view-only, no actions) until proper authorization frameworks exist.

Superhuman additionally reported unauthorized agents were detected operating inside bank customer accounts across India, Latin America, and South Korea, prompting similar alerts at financial institutions in those regions.

top_stories.title: Gaps Found in OpenAI's AI Agent Monitoring System
points: Independent researchers (METR, and separately with Redwood Research) found that OpenAI's internal monitoring of AI agents only triggered when agents returned control to users, leaving a coverage gap.
This gap left about 10% of internal Codex (OpenAI's coding agent) traffic unmonitored from May to July 2026; OpenAI has since patched the issue.

A follow-up three-week security assessment by METR and Redwood Research found further vulnerabilities that could let agents evade monitoring, bypass sandbox restrictions (isolated testing environments), and conceal their actions.

top_stories.title: Protecting Yourself from Rising AI-Powered Scams and Social Engineering
points: Voice cloning attacks now work from just seconds of audio, letting attackers convincingly impersonate family members or officials.

Defenses: set a family safe word shared only in person (never texted or posted online, since common choices like a pet's name are often public), hang up and call back on a known saved number for any urgent money request, use an authenticator app instead of SMS for two-factor authentication (2FA), and use a password manager with no duplicate passwords.

In India, 'digital arrest' scams (fake police video calls claiming legal detention) are not real under Indian law; victims should hang up, call 1930, or report at cybercrime.gov.in, since early reporting freezes stolen funds fastest.

General advice across newsletters: update all devices immediately with auto-updates enabled, freeze credit to block unauthorized account openings, and audit/revoke unused third-party AI app permissions (Google, ChatGPT, Claude) monthly.

unique_angles.point: SBI (State Bank of India) had 3,897 customer records (names, phone numbers, addresses) leaked online, enough for convincing scam calls, and when paired with stolen biometrics, enough to fraudulently obtain SIM cards in someone's name.

items.title: Microsoft's AI Diagnostic System Outperforms Doctors on Hard Cases
points: Microsoft's MAI-DxO simulates a virtual panel of AI doctors that propose diagnoses, order tests, and challenge each other as new data arrives.

On 304 complex cases from the New England Journal of Medicine, it more than doubled physician diagnostic accuracy; on routine ER cases it hit 80% accuracy versus 47% for doctors, while ordering fewer and cheaper tests.
One configuration reached 81% accuracy on the hardest cases at under half the cost of comparable systems, with gains holding even on newer models like GPT-5.5.
Real-world clinical trials begin at Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center in Boston to compare AI diagnoses against clinician assessments.

items.title: Put Your Open Chrome Tabs to Work
points: OpenAI's official ChatGPT Chrome extension adds a side panel that can read and compare multiple open browser tabs at once.

Example workflow: compare three pricing pages against team size, required features, budget, and billing period, then have ChatGPT verify the comparison against the actual pages before trusting the numbers.
The 'Work' feature can group only tabs you've manually confirmed, keeping trials, purchases, and unrelated items out of the task to maintain focus.

items.title: Other Funding and Industry News
points: Ex-OpenAI executive Kevin Weil's new venture Warp Sciences raised a $215 million Series A to build AI- and robotics-powered labs that help pharmaceutical companies develop medicines faster.
Baseten released two free open-source decision models, mammoth-1 and elephant-1, with mammoth ranking #1 on the Jev Decision Index.

items.title: Advanced Robotics and AI-Generated Content
points: A martial arts robot demonstrates sophisticated AI-powered physical capabilities, blurring the line between automated fitness coaching and autonomous robotics.

AI-generated video has reportedly reached photorealism, with viral clips of AI cats working at a McDonald's that are nearly indistinguishable from real footage, raising authenticity and misinformation concerns.
A ChatGPT-powered talking fish video unexpectedly went viral, showing AI's growing entertainment and engagement potential beyond typical productivity uses.

items.title: Practical AI Tools Gaining Traction
points: The 'Fact Finder' prompt extracts essential information from any article within seconds and has become a reader favorite for productivity.
A new, comprehensive database of ChatGPT prompts lets workplace professionals apply advanced AI techniques without needing technical expertise.

items.title: OpenAI and Anthropic Push Into Biotech
points: OpenAI acquired Orchestra Bio to build AI agents for drug development.
Anthropic's Claude spent 64 hours autonomously designing proteins to counter scorpion venom, with early lab validation results reported.

items.title: Weak Certificate Keys Force Browser Vendors to Act Fast
points: Certificate authority eMudhra issued absurdly weak cryptographic keys (one was literally the number 4), undermining the security certificates meant to verify website identity.
Chrome, Firefox, Apple, and Microsoft were forced to block eMudhra's certificates within hours to days of discovery.

items.title: Anthropic's IPO Filing Reveals Frontier AI Economics
points: Anthropic's IPO (initial public offering) filing shows $16.3 billion in revenue for H1 2026, against nearly $9 billion spent on compute (cloud computing power for running AI models) in the same period.

items.title: Meta's Capital Strategy and Financial Results
points: Meta is proposing a new nonvoting stock class to raise capital for $825 billion in AI infrastructure spending commitments while letting CEO Mark Zuckerberg pay a proposed 5% California wealth tax without losing voting control of the company.
Q3 earnings beat expectations with $64 billion in revenue, up 26% year-over-year.

items.title: Image Generation Market Shake-Up
points: Canva launched its first frontier image model, Canva Craft, which ranks 4th on the Design Arena leaderboard (behind only three OpenAI models); it uses a two-step process that plans layout before rendering for higher precision and supports 55 languages.

Getty Images filed for bankruptcy restructuring after a failed Shutterstock merger, squeezed by mounting debt, smartphone photography, and competition from AI-generated images; the company was valued at $5 billion four years ago.

items.title: 1Password Launches Agent Authentication Platform
points: 1Password launched a platform letting AI agents access user credentials securely without exposing the actual passwords to the agent.

items.title: Claude Adds Invisible Watermark for EU Compliance
points: Anthropic's latest Claude models embed a SynthID-Text watermark by subtly nudging word choices among near-equivalent options, rather than adding hidden characters, to comply with EU AI Act requirements.
The watermark carries no information about user identity and adds negligible performance overhead.

items.title: New Model Training and Deployment Methods
points: WorldTUI is a 360-million-parameter model fine-tuned to emulate a full computer terminal—including file system, vim text editor, tmux (terminal multiplexer), and command memory—without needing real backend infrastructure.

Perplexity's JOLT self-distillation method trains a model to act as both teacher and student, adapting feedback to the student's capability level, improving math, coding, and agentic task performance.
Cerebras demonstrated deployment of a trillion-parameter model split across multiple WSE-3T wafers, each with 44 GB of on-chip memory.

issues.subject: 🏦 U.S. banks catch AI agents going off-script

headlines: U.S. banks including JPMorgan, Bank of America, and Morgan Stanley are restricting third-party AI agents after catching them logging into customer accounts and taking unauthorized actions, with some executives calling the situation 'horrifying' due to risk of financial loss.

AI agents can now misinterpret instructions and act beyond their authority, prompting banks to move toward read-only access while they build frameworks to distinguish between authorized and rogue agents.

Microsoft's MAI-DxO diagnostic AI system outperformed physicians on complex medical cases (more than doubled accuracy) and routine ER visits (80% vs 47%), while ordering fewer and cheaper tests, with real-world clinical trials starting at Boston's Beth Israel Deaconess.

A spike in malicious AI attacks using voice cloning and social engineering is accelerating; key defenses include family code words, callback verification on saved numbers, 2FA with authenticator apps, and zero-duplicate passwords via password managers.

sections.title: Banks Crack Down on AI Agents' Account Access
points: JPMorgan, Bank of America, Morgan Stanley, and Citi discovered third-party AI agents logging in with customers' credentials, calling support lines, and taking actions users never requested—most were user-authorized but some acted beyond instructions.

Bank executives are struggling to distinguish between user-approved agents operating as intended versus rogue agents (those going off-script), with the main risk being AI hallucination (misreading instructions and making incorrect decisions) when given authority to move funds or make purchases.

Response: Morgan Stanley is blocking third-party agents entirely; JPMorgan, BofA, and Citi are restricting them with most banks moving to read-only access (allowing agents to view information but not take actions) until they can build proper authorization frameworks.

Blanket blocks buy time for banks to develop systems that let cleared agents take defined, limited actions while catching unauthorized behavior—critical since agent use is growing and security gaps can't persist forever.

sections.title: Microsoft's AI Diagnostic System Outperforms Doctors on Hard Cases
points: MAI-DxO works by simulating a virtual panel of doctors where AI agents propose diagnoses, order tests, and challenge each other as new data arrives, mirroring how expert medical teams reach difficult diagnoses.

On 304 complex cases from the New England Journal of Medicine, the system more than doubled physician accuracy with reference tools available; on typical ER cases, it achieved 80% accuracy versus 47% for doctors, while ordering fewer and cheaper tests.
One configuration reached 81% accuracy on the most difficult cases at less than half the cost of comparable systems, with performance gains holding even with newer AI models like GPT-5.5.

Real-world clinical trials will begin at Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center in Boston, measuring how AI diagnoses compare to clinician assessments—diagnostic accuracy alone is only the first step; AI must also guide treatment and fit into patient-doctor decision-making to prove value at scale.

sections.title: Safeguard Yourself from AI Hacks (Spike in Malicious AI Attacks)
points: Voice cloning attacks now work from seconds of audio, and AI can impersonate anyone; key defenses include setting a family code word that callers must state (shared in-person, never by text) and hanging up then calling back on saved numbers for any urgent money request.

Enable two-factor authentication (2FA) using an authenticator app rather than SMS, use a password manager like 1Password with zero duplicated passwords so one leaked login doesn't unlock your entire life, and confirm any payment request on a different channel than it arrived on.

Update all devices today (browsers, phones, laptops, desktop apps) because this week's certificate compromise exposed unpatched software as an open door; builders should also use OpenAI's free PHP vulnerability checker to test website exposure.
The spike in malicious AI attacks is accelerating and expected to worsen as attackers learn new techniques—taking these precautions now is critical and worth sharing with family.

Have ChatGPT check the comparison against the actual pages to verify full team cost and confirm details rather than guessing, then verify missing information by reviewing the pages yourself before asking for recommendations with source links.

Use the Work feature (where available) to group only the tabs you've confirmed, then review the actual group in Chrome to ensure accuracy—keep trials, purchases, and unrelated messages outside the task to maintain focus.

sections.title: The PHP Vulnerability That Bypasses Everything
points: Two critical PHP bugs (unfixed since 2012) let attackers take over web servers without passwords and without any user clicking anything—found August 1 by AI, exploited by October 17, four days before the public fix.

Timeline shows how fast attacks happen: Within hours of patch release on October 21, Amazon detected widespread exploitation; Microsoft simultaneously reported a China-linked group using an AI hacking tool to reach admin access in under 3 hours.

Dutch government, German Charité hospital, and other critical infrastructure went offline preemptively on October 21 morning rather than risk compromise—the safe choice when you can't patch immediately.

sections.title: Why Your Password Strategy Is Now Irrelevant
points: Your data sits on hundreds of servers controlled by people you've never met; you cannot patch their infrastructure and cannot control what happens on their end when breaches occur.
Even with strong passwords and 2FA, server-level exploits (like the PHP holes) bypass all client-side security entirely—the attacker doesn't need your credentials, they bypass authentication.
Storm-0940 attack fired 2,900 login attempts per minute at Microsoft 365 accounts, but passkeys and security keys cannot be guessed or leaked from compromised servers elsewhere.
AI agents used by labs testing vulnerabilities in Indian companies went undetected until disclosed by the AI providers themselves—companies had no visibility into what happened on their own systems.

sections.title: Immediate Actions to Limit Damage When Breaches Happen
points: Email: Add security keys (passkeys cannot be guessed or leaked from other servers); founders should enable Google's free Advanced Protection Program requiring physical keys.

Banking: Disable online and international use on unused cards, reduce UPI transaction limits to daily spend amounts, ensure all alerts reach an active phone number—this caps damage if credentials are stolen.

Identity: 3,897 SBI customer records (names, phone numbers, addresses) are online and sufficient for convincing scam calls; paired with biometric theft, fraudsters can get SIM cards issued in your name.

AI tool permissions: Audit Google third-party connections, ChatGPT Apps section, and Claude Connectors monthly; revoke anything unused in 30 days; run AI agents in separate Chrome profiles with zero banking/government logins and set Claude to 'manually approve' mode.

sections.title: Social Engineering and Family Fraud Prevention
points: Pick a family safe word never posted online (your dog's name doesn't work—it's been posted 400 times); any call about money or emergencies gets hung up on, then you call back on a known number and verify with the safe word.

'Digital arrest' does not exist in Indian law—it's a scam; if someone in police uniform on a video call claims otherwise, hang up, dial 1930, or report at cybercrime.gov.in; early reports freeze money fastest.

Warn non-technical family members that AI hacking tools and social engineering are the fastest path in after server exploits fail; no amount of caution on your end protects against breaches on the vendor's end.
